explanation: OEIS A104320: a(n) is the number of zeros in the ternary representation of 2^n; 'Conjecture from N. J. A. Sloane: a(n) > 0 for n > 15'. The formal a counts 0 in Nat.digits 3 (2^n) (no leading zeros), and the statement is a n > 0 for n > 15. I checked numerically that 2^n has a ternary 0 for 16 ≤ n < 3000. Faithful.
